basic_information.name: Botpress
basic_information.creator: Botpress Inc. (founded by Sylvain Perron; headquartered in Quebec City, Canada)
basic_information.description: Botpress is an open-core conversational AI platform that combines a visual flow editor with a GPT-native autonomous engine (LLMz) to let teams build, deploy, and manage intelligent chatbots and AI agents across multiple channels. Originally launched as a fully open-source chatbot framework in 2017, it pivoted to a cloud-first platform in 2023 while maintaining open-source roots. For entrepreneurs, Botpress offers a powerful free tier for prototyping customer support bots, lead qualification agents, and internal assistants, with a model-agnostic architecture that avoids LLM vendor lock-in and supports deployment on web, WhatsApp, Slack, Messenger, and custom apps.
basic_information.release_date: 2017 (open-source v12); 2023 (Botpress Cloud launch); June 2025 (Series B, latest major milestone)

technical_capabilities.underlying_models: Multi-provider via custom LLMz inference engine: supports OpenAI (GPT-4o, GPT-4, GPT-3.5), Anthropic (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3), Google (Gemini), Meta (Llama), Mistral, and other models. The LLMz engine standardizes tool calling and message formats across providers, allowing model swapping with minimal prompt changes. Studio exposes 'Best Model' and 'Fast Model' presets for easy configuration.
technical_capabilities.customization_depth: workflow-builder | code-extension. Botpress combines a visual drag-and-drop flow builder (Agent Studio) with an Autonomous Engine that blends generative AI with structured logic. Users can extend functionality through custom code actions (JavaScript/TypeScript), API calls, webhooks, and the Hub's integration library. Advanced users can build custom integrations and publish them to the Botpress Hub.
technical_capabilities.api_access: Yes. REST API and GraphQL API for bot management, conversation control, and data exchange. Every bot gets a live API endpoint. Webhook integration for event-driven automation. SDK available for custom integrations.
technical_capabilities.deployment_options: Cloud-hosted (primary, Botpress Cloud), embeddable webchat widget (JavaScript snippet for any website), self-hosted via Docker (v12 open-source version), multi-channel deployment (WhatsApp, Messenger, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Telegram, Twilio SMS, Line, Viber, custom apps via API). Enterprise plan offers on-premises and hybrid cloud options.
technical_capabilities.ai_model_flexibility: multi-provider | bring-your-own-model. The LLMz engine is model-agnostic, supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Mistral, and custom models. Users can switch models with minimal prompt changes. Enterprise customers can integrate self-hosted or custom LLMs.

user_experience.target_user: developer | business_user | enterprise_team. Botpress has a developer-first heritage but has evolved to serve non-technical builders through the visual Agent Studio. Best suited for technical product teams and developers who want deep customization, but increasingly accessible to business users for simpler use cases.
user_experience.learning_curve: hours. Basic chatbot with knowledge base achievable in 1-2 hours using visual builder and templates. Mastering advanced features (Autonomous Nodes, custom integrations, API calls, multi-agent workflows) takes days to weeks. Steeper learning curve than simpler alternatives like Chatbase or Tidio.
user_experience.setup_time: 15-30 minutes from signup to first working chatbot demo with knowledge base
user_experience.collaboration_features: Shared workspaces, role-based access controls (Team and Enterprise plans), multiple collaborators per bot (1 on free, 2 on Plus, 3 on Team), conversation history and analytics. Enterprise plan adds advanced team management and dedicated support.
user_experience.template_library: Botpress provides pre-built bot templates accessible from Studio (Recipe Bot, Recruitment Bot, AI Public Personality Bot, Cinema Booking, customer support, appointment scheduling, lead qualification). The Hub acts as a centralized marketplace for prebuilt workflows, integrations, and community-contributed assets. GitHub Solutions repository offers additional starter templates and custom modules.
user_experience.visual_builder_type: drag-drop | hybrid. Agent Studio provides a visual drag-and-drop flow builder for designing conversation paths. The Autonomous Engine adds AI-powered nodes that handle intent recognition, slot-filling, and fallback responses automatically. Users can combine visual flows with code blocks for hybrid development.

ai_and_rag_capabilities.rag_support: Built-in Knowledge Base with full RAG pipeline. Users upload documents (PDF, TXT, DOCX), websites, and other content sources. Botpress automatically chunks, vectorizes, and indexes content. The default Autonomous Node includes a Search Knowledge Card that queries all Knowledge Bases automatically. Supports visual knowledge base indexing (Plus plan and above). Vector DB storage: 100 MB (free), 1 GB (Plus), 2 GB (Team). File storage: 500 MB (free), 10 GB (Plus/Team).
ai_and_rag_capabilities.agent_capabilities: multi-step | autonomous. Botpress supports complex multi-step conversation workflows with the Autonomous Engine that blends generative AI with structured logic. Agents can connect to knowledge bases, integrate with enterprise tools, handle intent recognition, slot-filling, and fallback responses. The platform positions itself as a full-stack AI agent development framework, not just a chatbot builder.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.model_selection: Multi-vendor. Users select between 'Best Model' and 'Fast Model' presets in Studio. The LLMz engine supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Mistral, and custom models. Enterprise customers can bring their own models (BYOM). Model swapping requires minimal prompt changes thanks to the standardized LLMz engine.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.prompt_management: Built-in prompt configuration for each node with system prompts, personality settings, and response instructions. The Autonomous Engine manages prompt optimization internally. Botpress Academy provides courses on prompt optimization for RAG and agent behavior.

integration_and_ecosystem.key_integrations: WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Telegram, Instagram, Twilio (SMS), Line, Viber, Vonage, HubSpot, Salesforce (via API), Zendesk, Intercom, Notion, Zapier, Trello, Pipedrive, Klaviyo, MailerLite, Google Analytics (via API), Webhook. Enterprise integrations with CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce), helpdesk (Zendesk, Intercom), ERP (Oracle, SAP via API), and marketing automation (Mailchimp).
integration_and_ecosystem.integration_count: 20+ direct integrations via the Botpress Hub, plus hundreds more through Zapier, custom webhooks, and REST/GraphQL APIs. Community can contribute and publish custom integrations to the Hub.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_support: Yes. Botpress has an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that connects AI agents like Claude, Cursor, and Windsurf directly to Botpress accounts. Supports conversation management, bot issue tracking, and workspace discovery. Available via Composio and other MCP integration platforms.
integration_and_ecosystem.webhook_support: Yes. Built-in webhook integration generates a personalized webhook URL for each bot. Supports inbound webhooks (receive external triggers) with x-bp-secret header authentication, and outbound API calls from conversation flows.
integration_and_ecosystem.export_formats: Embeddable webchat widget (JavaScript snippet), API endpoint (every bot gets a callable REST endpoint), webhook triggers, multi-channel deployment (WhatsApp, Messenger, Slack, Teams, etc.). The v12 open-source version allows full code export and self-hosting. Cloud version is primarily SaaS-based with embed and API access.

pricing_and_accessibility.pricing_model: freemium + usage-based. Four tiers: Pay-as-You-Go (free), Plus, Team, Enterprise. Base subscription fee plus separate AI Spend (usage-based cost for LLM token consumption). Monthly AI credit included, with additional AI Spend billed separately.
pricing_and_accessibility.free_tier_limits: Pay-as-You-Go plan ($0/month): 500 incoming messages/events, 1 bot, 1 collaborator, 100 MB vector DB, 500 MB file storage, $5 monthly AI credit, visual building studio, conversation history, community support. AI Spend capped at $100/month. Monthly limits reset at 05:00 GMT.
pricing_and_accessibility.paid_plans: Plus: $89/month + AI Spend ($79/month billed annually), 5,000 messages, 2 bots, 2 collaborators, 1 GB vector DB, 10 GB file storage, live agent handoff, visual KB indexing, Always Alive for 1 bot. Team: $495/month + AI Spend, 50,000 messages, 3 bots, 3 collaborators, 2 GB vector DB, role-based access, advanced support, Always Alive for 3 bots, AI Spend cap $500/month. Enterprise: starting ~$2,000/month (3-year term), custom limits, custom AI Spend, SOC 2, dedicated support, on-premises options.
pricing_and_accessibility.open_source: open-core. Botpress v12 is fully open-source under AGPLv3 (self-hostable). Current Botpress Cloud SDK and integrations are MIT-licensed on GitHub. The cloud platform itself is proprietary SaaS. Dual-licensed: AGPLv3 + Botpress Proprietary License for v12; MIT for current open-source components.
pricing_and_accessibility.self_hosting_option: Available via Botpress v12 (open-source, AGPLv3). Supports Docker deployment and custom server hosting. However, v12 lacks the newer AI/LLM features of Botpress Cloud. Cloud platform does not offer self-hosting for standard plans; Enterprise plan provides on-premises and hybrid cloud options.
pricing_and_accessibility.data_residency_and_sovereignty: GDPR compliant with appointed Data Protection Officer and EU Data Protection Representative. SOC 2 compliant (monitored via Drata). Data is stored in the US by default. International transfers use EU-US Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses. European data localization is actively in progress but not yet available as of early 2026. Enterprise customers can negotiate specific data residency arrangements. No explicit EU AI Act readiness certification yet.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the open-source/open-core chatbot builder category. Botpress occupies a unique position as a developer-friendly yet increasingly no-code platform, sitting between fully proprietary builders (Voiceflow, Chatbase) and purely developer-centric frameworks (Rasa). Strong in enterprise and mid-market segments, with growing adoption among solo builders and startups since the cloud platform launch in 2023.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Fortune 500 companies and enterprises including Kia, Electronic Arts (EA), Husqvarna, Windstream, Shell. Case study: RubyLabs/Able reduced support tickets by 60-65% using Botpress AI agent with zero hallucinations. Used by startups, nonprofits, and government organizations worldwide.
adoption_and_market.community_size: ~14,000 GitHub stars (main repository), 88 repositories on GitHub. Over 100,000 developers have used the platform. Active Discord community. Botpress Hub hosts community-contributed integrations and templates. Millions of automated conversations per month across the platform.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: ~$40M across multiple rounds. Series A: $15M (April 2021, led by Decibel Partners with Inovia Capital). Series B: $25M (June 2025, led by Framework Venture Partners with participation from HubSpot Ventures, Deloitte Ventures, Inovia Capital). 13 total investors. Valuation not publicly disclosed.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: Voiceflow (more designer-friendly, stronger visual prototyping, credit-based pricing), Dialogflow CX (Google, enterprise NLU, complex setup), Rasa (fully open-source, Python-based, more developer-heavy, 20K+ GitHub stars), Chatbase (simpler, cheaper, better for beginners), Tidio (e-commerce focused), Intercom Fin (enterprise customer support). Botpress differentiates through: model-agnostic LLMz engine, open-core approach, visual + code hybrid, strong multi-channel support, and autonomous AI agent capabilities.
adoption_and_market.ecosystem_lock_in_risk: low-medium. Open-core model with MIT-licensed SDK and integrations. v12 is fully open-source (AGPLv3) and self-hostable. Cloud platform has proprietary elements but bots can be deployed via API endpoints, making migration feasible. However, complex flows built in Agent Studio are not directly portable to competing platforms. The model-agnostic LLMz engine reduces AI vendor lock-in.

teaching_and_classroom.class_project_idea:
Project 1: 'AI Customer Support Agent for a Startup' (60 min) - Students sign up for the free Pay-as-You-Go plan, create a chatbot for a fictional French startup (e.g., a food delivery service or SaaS product). They upload 3-5 FAQ documents to the Knowledge Base, configure the AI agent's personality and instructions in French, design a conversation flow with greeting, FAQ handling via RAG, and escalation to human agent. They embed the bot on a test page using the webchat widget. Deliverable: working chatbot URL + 2-slide pitch on how it reduces support costs and improves response time.

Project 2: 'Multi-Channel Lead Qualification Bot' (75 min) - Students build an AI agent that qualifies leads for a B2B product. They design a multi-step flow that asks qualifying questions (company size, budget, pain points), uses conditional logic to score leads (hot/warm/cold), and routes qualified leads via webhook to a simulated CRM. Students deploy the bot to Webchat and explore the WhatsApp/Slack channel options. Deliverable: working agent demo + analysis of automation ROI vs. hiring a sales development representative (SDR).

teaching_and_classroom.student_prerequisites: nothing | basic prompting. No coding required for basic bot building in the visual Studio. Understanding of basic prompting concepts (how to write clear AI instructions) is helpful for configuring the Autonomous Engine and Knowledge Base. No Python or JavaScript knowledge needed for core features.
teaching_and_classroom.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools) - primary fit. Students use Botpress to build a working AI chatbot, applying prompt engineering concepts to configure agent personality and RAG responses. Also relevant to Session 3 (AI Project Frameworks) for Build vs Buy analysis (comparing Botpress free tier vs custom development), and Session 4 (Business Models) for analyzing chatbot-as-a-service and usage-based pricing models.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Botpress is ideal for early-stage startups (pre-seed to Series A) with 1-5 person teams who need to deploy AI-powered customer interactions quickly. Best use cases: (1) Customer support automation - deploy a knowledge-base-powered chatbot in days to handle FAQ, reducing ticket volume by 50-65% (as demonstrated by RubyLabs/Able case study); (2) Lead qualification and onboarding - automate repetitive sales conversations across web, WhatsApp, and Messenger; (3) Internal tools - build employee-facing assistants for HR, IT, or operations documentation. The free tier (500 messages/month, 1 bot) is sufficient for early validation. Graduate to Plus ($89/month) when moving to production. Particularly valuable for teams that want more control than simpler tools like Chatbase offer, but lack the engineering resources for a fully custom Rasa deployment.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_mvp: 1-3 days for a basic customer support chatbot with knowledge base and webchat embed. 1-2 weeks for a polished multi-channel agent with custom flows, API integrations, and webhook triggers. The visual builder plus pre-built templates accelerate initial setup. The Autonomous Engine reduces the need for manually designing every conversation path, speeding up iteration significantly.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Botpress when: you need multi-channel chatbot deployment (web + WhatsApp + Slack), you want model-agnostic AI flexibility, you need more customization than simple chatbot builders offer, or you value the open-core approach for future self-hosting. Build custom when: you need deep integration with proprietary NLP pipelines, have unique performance/latency requirements, or your conversation volume makes usage-based pricing uneconomical (100K+ messages/month). Consider alternatives: Voiceflow for more designer-friendly visual prototyping; Rasa for full open-source control with Python; Chatbase for simpler, faster setup at lower cost. Cost comparison: Botpress free tier handles validation; Plus at $89/month + AI Spend is cheaper than a developer hire for low-to-medium volume; at high volume, the usage-based AI Spend component requires careful unit economics modeling.
key_lessons: 1. Start with Knowledge Base, not complex flows: Upload your existing documentation and let the RAG-powered Autonomous Engine handle most queries automatically. Only build custom conversation flows for high-value interactions that need precise control. This gets you to a useful MVP in hours, not weeks.

2. Watch the AI Spend: Botpress's pricing splits into base subscription + AI Spend (token consumption). The base plan may seem affordable, but AI Spend can grow unpredictably with complex conversations and large knowledge bases. Model your cost-per-conversation early and set AI Spend alerts.

3. Leverage the model-agnostic engine: Unlike platforms locked to GPT, Botpress's LLMz engine lets you switch between OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, and Mistral with minimal changes. Use cheaper/faster models for simple queries and premium models for complex interactions to optimize costs.

4. Plan your channel strategy from day one: Botpress's strength is multi-channel deployment (web, WhatsApp, Messenger, Slack, Teams). Deploy where your customers already are rather than forcing them to visit your website. Each channel has different user expectations - design accordingly.

5. Consider the open-core graduation path: If you outgrow the cloud platform or need full data control, Botpress v12 (AGPLv3) allows self-hosting. This is a unique advantage over fully proprietary alternatives. Document your conversation logic and integration points to keep your migration options open.

confidence.data_quality: High. Information sourced from official Botpress documentation, Botpress Academy, GitHub repository, reputable review platforms (G2, GetApp, Capterra), funding databases (Crunchbase, Tracxn), multiple independent review sites (Chatimize, eesel AI, Lindy, BigSur AI), and competitor analysis pages (Voiceflow, GPTBots).
confidence.cross_reference: Pricing confirmed across Botpress official site, eesel AI, Lindy, GPTBots, BigSur AI, and G2. Funding data confirmed via Crunchbase, Tracxn, PitchBook, and Botpress blog. Feature set verified through official docs, Botpress Academy, GitHub repository, and multiple third-party reviews. Customer case studies confirmed via Botpress customer stories page.
confidence.caveats: AI Spend costs can be unpredictable and are not fully transparent in advance, making total cost of ownership difficult to estimate before deployment. The platform has undergone a major architectural shift from self-hosted v12 to cloud-first, so some older open-source community resources reference the deprecated v12 architecture. EU data residency is not yet available (in progress as of early 2026). The free tier's 500 messages/month is very limited for realistic production testing. Botpress v12 (self-hosted) lacks many newer AI/LLM features available only on the cloud platform, creating a gap between the open-source and proprietary offerings. GitHub star count (~14K) is approximate and may have changed.
